title: Sabha: Indraprastha
hook: Narada adds a warning to Pandu's request and leaves; everyone says yes, and Yudhishthira sends for Krishna
carry: send for the one who sees further

segments.voice: Yesterday, a father's words in the sabha: Pandu, through Narada, asking his son to perform the Rajasuya — "tell my son," he said. Did you pass on a kind word? Day seven hundred fifty-one.

Narada has one more thing to say before he goes. This sacrifice, he tells the king, is hard to finish. It has many obstacles. Brahma-rakshasas, demons who haunt sacrifices, look for any flaw in it. And after it, a war can come, one that destroys the warriors of the earth. Think it over, Narada says. Do what's good for you. And then he leaves, and the hall is left holding both halves of the message.
screen: `HARD TO FINISH.` → `DEMONS LOOK FOR FLAWS.` → `A WAR CAN COME AFTER.`

segments.voice: Put the two halves side by side. A dead father asking his son to rise to this. A sage warning that it might end in ruin. Yudhishthira doesn't brush either one aside. The text says he sighed, and thought, and couldn't find peace. So he does what a king in a sabha is supposed to do. He asks. First his ministers and his brothers. They all say the same thing: you deserve this, the time is right, do it. Then he asks the priests and sages around him, Dhaumya, and Vyasa himself. They agree too. Everyone in the room says yes. And still Yudhishthira doesn't move. The text gives his reasoning. People who love you, he thinks, don't always point out the danger. Some say what pleases. Some are carried along by their own hopes. So he thinks of one person who sees further, who won't flatter him, and who knows the world: Krishna. He sends a fast messenger to Dwaraka, and Krishna comes, quickly, to Indraprastha. So a unanimous yes doesn't end his asking. Yudhishthira isn't looking for a no. He's looking for someone who will tell him the truth, either way. A sabha, after all, is a room full of counsel. The best use of it is knowing whose counsel you most need. This is the last day of the hall's own story, the sabha at Indraprastha. Everything from here leans toward the sacrifice. Tomorrow, Krishna gives his answer, and the Rajasuya begins to take shape.
screen: `A REQUEST AND A WARNING.` · `EVERYONE SAYS YES.` · `LOVE DOESN'T ALWAYS SEE DANGER.` · `SEND FOR THE ONE WHO SEES FURTHER.` · then, large: `A UNANIMOUS YES IS NOT AN ANSWER.`

segments.voice: Let the breath slow. Bring to mind a decision in front of you, large or small. Notice who has already told you yes. Then ask yourself, quietly: who would tell me the truth about this, even if it isn't what I want to hear? Let a face come. You don't have to call them. Just know who it is, and breathe with that. The bell holds the time.
Sabha. A hall full of counsel. Today, every voice in it says yes, and the king still sends for one more.
Your line: send for the one who sees further. Today, before you settle something that matters, ask one person who won't simply agree. Day seven hundred fifty-one.

howItsDone: Hindu tradition remembers Krishna in the Mahabharata as a counselor as well as a god, and his advice to the Pandavas is often retold alongside the story of the Rajasuya.

match.prompt: the warning and the counsel — tap the pairs.

original.note: Sanskrit nārada: the wandering sage who brings Pandu's request and the warning, then leaves.

trapdoor: what you thought: a king being talked into a big party.
what it means: a king weighing a father's request against a sage's warning, and seeking honest counsel.
what a scholar hears: the text gives Yudhishthira's own reasoning, that friends may say what pleases, before he sends for Krishna.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Sabha Parva, Lokapala Sabhakhyana Parva (Narada's warning) and Rajasuyarambha Parva (Yudhishthira consults ministers, brothers, Dhaumya and Vyasa, and sends for Krishna)

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm Narada's warning: many obstacles, Brahma-rakshasas seeking flaws, and a war destroying kshatriyas after the sacrifice.
Confirm Yudhishthira consults ministers and brothers, then Dhaumya and Dvaipayana (Vyasa), who all approve.
Confirm Yudhishthira's reasoning that friends may not point out faults out of affection or self-interest before he sends for Krishna.
Confirm Krishna is sent for at Dwaraka (Dwaravati) and comes quickly.
